title: CLCON/313/2015 of Mohammad Imran Vs D.s. Garbiyal AND ANOTHER

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Civil Contempt Petition No. 313 of 2015
Mohammad Imran ................ Petitioner

versus
D.S. Garbiyal & another ................ Respondents
Mr. N.S. Pundir, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. R.C. Arya, Standing Counsel for the State / opposite parties.

U.C. Dhyani, J.(Oral)
By means of present civil contempt petition, the
petitioner seeks to summon the respondents in person and
punish them for deliberately disobeying the order dated
20.11.2014, passed by this Court in Writ Petition no. 364
(S/B) of 2014, Mohammad Imran vs State of
Uttarakhand and others, under the Contempt of Court
Act.
2) On 20.11.2014, in WPSB no. 364 of 2014, this
Court passed the following order:
 "In view of the documents given by the
petitioner and submission made therein, we dispose of
the matter with the following direction.
 The petitioner is given the liberty to be present
before the High Level Committee with all his
documents, including his document relating to his
administrative experience, and the Committee, which is
so constituted, will examine the candidature of the
petitioner and if it finds that the petitioner is working at

2
a Pay Grade of Rs. 5400 and has all the other
qualifications, as required, they shall consider the
candidature of the petitioner in accordance with his
merit.
 Meanwhile, we also direct that this high level
committee, shall also scrutinize the entire list of the
candidates which was before the scrutiny Committee
and if it in its wisdom finds that any candidate, who is
required to be cleared has not been cleared, then it shall
do so, but after seeking explanation from the Scrutiny
Committee. This is being directed so that other eligible
candidates may also have an opportunity to participate
in the selection process, in case they have been
wrongly rejected, considering that it is not a very long
list of candidates."
3) A direction was, therefore, given to the High
Level Committee to examine the candidature of the
petitioner and if it finds that the petitioner is working at a
Pay Grade of Rs. 5400 and has all the other
qualifications, as required, they shall consider the
candidature of the petitioner in accordance with his merit.
A direction was also given to the High Level Committee
to scrutinize the entire list of the candidates which was
before the scrutiny committee and if it in its wisdom finds
that any candidate, who is required to be cleared has not
been cleared, then it shall do so, but after seeking
explanation from the scrutiny committee. A further
direction was also given to the other eligible candidates

3
to have an opportunity to participate in the selection
process if their case has been wrongly rejected.
4) Counter affidavit has been filed on behalf of
the respondent no. 2 narrating all the facts and annexing
the office memorandum, whereby High Level Committee
was constituted in compliance of the order of the Court.
Annexure-3 to the counter affidavit has been filed to
show that Mohd. Imran, Law Officer, Uttarakhand
Agriculture Produce and Marketing Board, Rudrapur has
been appointed, on deputation, on the post of Sahayak
Nagar Adhikari, Nagar Nigam, Dehradun.
5) Thus, the compliance of the order passed by
the Division Bench of this Court on 20.11.2014 has been
done in view of such compliance affidavit.
6) It is the submission of learned counsel for the
petitioner that the petitioner applied for the post of
Executive Officer in the Nagar Palika in pursuance to
advertisement dated 21.12.2013 and instead of granting
him appointment on the post of Executive Officer he was
appointed on the post of Sahayak Nagar Adhikari in the
Nagar Nigam, whereas the parent Department of the
petitioner has also given NOC to the petitioner for
appointment, on deputation, on the post of Executive
Officer, Nagar Palika.
7) It may be mentioned here that no direction as
such as is being claimed by learned counsel for the

4
petitioner was made by the Division Bench of this Court
while passing the order dated 20.11.2014. The Court
enforcing a decision will only look into the matter in the
background of the order which was passed by the Court.
In the contempt petition, the Court has not to see as to
what was the prayer of the petitioner, but has to see what
was directed by the Court. Since the order dated
20.11.2014 has been complied with, this Court does not
see any reason to proceed with the contempt petition, in
view of the compliance affidavit filed on behalf of the
respondents.
8) Contempt proceedings are hereby closed. It
will be open to the petitioner to seek appropriate remedy
before the appropriate forum against the petitioner's
appointment, on deputation, on the post of Sahayak
Nagar Adhikari, Nagar Nigam, if he is so advised.
